section.name: Overview
section.p: HtmlUnit has good support for JavaScript, which is continuously improved. Test cases for complex libraries (Dojo, htmx, jQuery, Prototype, Google Web Toolkit, Yahoo User Interface, and Sarissa) are already included. However, not all test cases pass, and you may encounter issues with real-world applications.

Before reporting a JavaScript issue, please try to isolate the root cause to a single JavaScript property or method. Simply stating that jQuery or a specific website is not working does not provide enough actionable information.

To find the offending line, insert alert() statements at various places and compare HtmlUnit's behavior against a real browser (Chrome, Firefox, or Edge). In most cases, you will be able to produce a minimal failing test case containing just a few lines of JavaScript independent of large external libraries. Please refer to some sample test cases.
Once the root cause is identified, it can usually be resolved in a timely manner. If you need help tracing an issue, please don't hesitate to ask the development team.

section.name: Suggested Steps
section.p: The first step is establishing a way to compare HtmlUnit's behavior against a real browser. This is easiest when using an intercepting proxy to modify incoming web content and inject debugging statements. One popular option is Charles Proxy.
Ensure you can modify the content and that the real browser does not serve cached responses:
Ensure you are configuring HtmlUnit with the same simulated BrowserVersion as the real browser being tested.
You may encounter an error similar to:
section.source: org.htmlunit.corejs.javascript.EcmaError: TypeError: Cannot call method "getAttribute" of undefined (http://download.dojotoolkit.org/release-1.4.0/dojo-release-1.4.0/dojo/dojo.js#16(eval)#16)
section.p: This indicates that in some_variable.getAttribute(), some_variable evaluated to undefined during execution.
Once the problematic line is located, trace up the call stack to identify where the behavior diverges.

To quickly iterate, save the web file locally and use your proxy's local mapping feature (known as Map Local in Charles) to override the remote response. You can also use online formatting tools to beautify minified JavaScript code.
Always test using the latest release version, or ideally the latest snapshot build.
